title: North‑Star thermostat: initiative capacity guardrails and cross‑company cadence
creator: Victor Chen
description: Problem: teams are over-committing into the roadmap and org-level OKRs are being diluted. Goal: create an operational 'North‑Star thermostat' — a lightweight decision and tooling pattern that (1) quantifies capacity vs committed initiative effort, (2) enforces gating for new initiatives against OKR priorities, and (3) prescribes escalation/ rebalance playbooks when the thermostat exceeds thresholds. Outcome: clearer initiative prioritization, fewer mid-cycle scope shifts, and measurable improvement in OKR completion rates.
acceptance_criteria: Thermostat metric defined and documented: velocity-utilization ratio (VUR) with computation examples
Gating rubric published: thresholds for green/yellow/red and decision owners for each band
Roadmap intake flow updated to include VUR check and mandatory OKR mapping for new initiatives
Console prototype: single-pane capacity view showing committed points by team, active OKR coverage, and thermostat band
Pilot completed with 3 cross-functional initiatives and retro captured; measurable reduction in scope churn vs previous cycle
tasks: Define metric (VUR) with input signals: team sprint velocity, planned initiative points, and cross-functional dependencies
Draft gating rubric and decision matrix (PM/Eng/Design/Reliability signoffs)
Update intake template in Confluence and roadmap intake form (Drive) to require OKR linkage
Frontend: design capacity view mockups and add telemetry hooks (Console) — track committed points per route/model
Backend: add API to compute VUR from workload CDRs and schedule aggregation jobs
Pilot run: coordinate with ENG-22411, DES-1782, and SRE for rollout and measurement
Write playbook for escalation and capacity reallocation (who to call, SLAs, rollback signals)
